title: Stalk of the transform at the origin of the dual line
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a Weil complex on $\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ (in the
conventions of [def-fd-transform]) and let $0'$ be the origin of
the dual line $V^\vee$. In the compact-support convention of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] there is a canonical
isomorphism

$$
\bigl(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\bigr)_{0'}\;\cong\;R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},K\bigr)[1].
$$

In particular, for the middle extension
$K=j_{!*}\mathcal M[1]=j_*\mathcal M[1]$ of a lisse sheaf
$\mathcal M$ on $U_0\subset\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, the stalk at
$0'$ has exactly two possibly nonzero cohomology groups, in degrees
$-1$ and $0$:

$$
\mathcal H^{-1}\bigl(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_*\mathcal M[1])_{0'}\bigr)
\cong H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M),
\qquad
\mathcal H^0\bigl(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_*\mathcal M[1])_{0'}\bigr)
\cong H_c^2(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M).
$$

proof.text: Apply [lem-fd-stalk-formula] with rank $r=1$ and the $k$-valued geometric point above the rational origin $0'$. Its fibre is $\mathbf A^1_k$ and its pairing function is $x\cdot0=0$. By [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf], the covering for the zero function is $T^p-T=0$: its components $T=a$, $a\in\mathbf F_p$, identify it with the trivial $\mathbf F_p$-torsor. The $\Psi$-isotypic part of its constant regular representation is the constant line, generated by the character vector with components $\Psi(a)$ (with the pullback action specified there). The component $T=0$ fixes its normalization, also over $k_0$. Thus the tensor kernel is the constant unit. The stalk formula consequently gives $R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1_k,\operatorname{For}K)[1]$, where [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] supplies exactly this geometric-fibre and forgetful convention for the displayed notation over $k_0$.

By [def-wf-middle-extension], $j$ is a dense open immersion and $j_*\mathcal M$ is the ordinary sheaf direct image. The affine line is a separated smooth geometrically connected affine curve: its geometric coordinate ring is $k[x]$, an integral polynomial ring of dimension one. Apply [lem-a1-adic-middle-extension-constructible] with $C_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal M$ to obtain the constructible Weil sheaf $A=j_*\mathcal M$ in degree zero. Thus [lem-zl-affine-curve-range] applies to $A$ and gives $H_c^i(\mathbf A^1_k,A)=0$ outside $\{0,1,2\}$. Apply [lem-a1-middle-extension-hc0] to this dense-open lisse input to remove degree zero as well. Substituting $K=A[1]$ into step 1 and commuting the derived cohomology functor with shifts yields $R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1_k,A)[2]$. In the convention of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], its degree $n$ cohomology is $H_c^{n+2}(\mathbf A^1_k,A)$. Hence only degrees $-1$ and $0$ can survive and their groups are respectively $H_c^1$ and $H_c^2$, as asserted.

I also read the statement of every cited node, the unit sk-p-dl-a1-perverse, and the blueprint text in both snapshots (master and main-20261015 agree). In Milne LEC I checked Definition 18.1 on pp.118-119 and Remark 29.7 on p.166. The item's statement is unchanged. Step 1: the stalk formula with r=1 at the rational origin has pairing 0. The Artin-Schreier covering for f=0 splits into p components. The vector (Psi(a)) spans the Psi-isotypic line, so the kernel is the constant unit, and RGamma_c follows from the geometric-fibre convention. Step 2: A^1 meets the hypotheses of the constructibility lemma, which gives j_*M constructible in degree 0. The range lemma then gives vanishing outside degrees 0..2, the new lemma removes H_c^0, and the shift by [2] leaves H_c^1 and H_c^2 in degrees -1 and 0. The new lemma is true: a compactly supported section is a section of a locally constant sheaf on a connected U, so its support is empty or U, and the closure of U is the non-proper affine C. Tests: A^1 with constant F, G_m inside A^1, F with no invariants, and F=0 all give 0. The affine hypothesis is necessary, since P^1 gives a nonzero group. The new lemma does not restate the item. It is the narrow H_c^0 clause of the unsplit lem-a1-middle-extension-endpoints and generalizes lem-a1-affine-hc0, which assumes F lisse on all of C. No exact duplicate exists. I accept both declared tool_uses. The range lemma is on the unit's route through sk-l-dl-a1-endpoints. The constructibility lemma from sk-i-dl-a1-local is a generic black-box check of a hypothesis.
